## Kyoto 4-Day Slow-Travel Plan
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/geo-alt.svg

A relaxed Kyoto trip works best with one anchor sight per day, short transit hops, and early starts for the busiest places. I’ve kept this plan centered on temple/garden highlights, food experiences, and one low-walking evening.

## Day-by-Day Kyoto Itinerary
### Day 1 — April 10: Higashiyama + Gion
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/building.svg
- Morning: Kiyomizu-dera early, then a slow walk through Sannenzaka and Ninenzaka before crowds build.
- Afternoon: Lunch in Higashiyama, then Maruyama Park and Yasaka Shrine area at an easy pace.
Media: Image=https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/f/f8/A199_Japan_Kyoto_Maruyama_Park_Gion_Ar%C3%A9a_%284764445344%29.jpg Alt=Afternoon: Lunch in Higashiyama, then Maruyama Park and Yasaka Shrine area at an easy pace, Kyoto, Japan
- Food: Tea and sweets tasting near Gion; add a matcha dessert stop.
- Evening: Keep it light with dinner in Gion and a short riverside stroll only.

Estimated local transport for 2: **JPY 1,500–2,500**
Best balance: Pair the famous temple with quieter side streets and avoid overpacking the day.
Media: Alt=Best balance: Pair the famous temple with quieter side streets and avoid overpacking the day, Kyoto, Japan

### Day 2 — April 11: Arashiyama + Zen Garden Time
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/tree.svg
- Morning: Tenryu-ji and its garden, then the bamboo grove very early if you want softer crowds.
- Afternoon: Choose one calmer add-on: Okochi Sanso Garden or a slow café break by the river.
- Food: Lunch with tofu cuisine or yudofu, which fits the area well.
- Evening: Return to central Kyoto for an easy dinner; keep walking minimal after sunset.

Estimated local transport for 2: **JPY 2,000–3,200**
Best balance: If the bamboo grove feels too busy, spend more time in Tenryu-ji’s garden or Okochi Sanso instead.

### Day 3 — April 12: Northern Kyoto Gardens + Nishiki Food Focus
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/cup-hot.svg
- Morning: Kinkaku-ji as the main sight, then move on rather than lingering too long.
- Afternoon: Swap in a quieter option such as Ryoan-ji’s rock garden if you want a more contemplative pace.
- Food: Nishiki Market tasting walk with small bites, pickles, tofu, sweets, and seasonal snacks.
Media: Image=https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/e/e5/A_store_at_Nishiki_market%2C_Kyoto%2C_Japan.jpg Alt=Food: Nishiki Market tasting walk with small bites, pickles, tofu, sweets, and seasonal snacks, Kyoto, Japan
- Evening: Make this your minimal-walking night: dinner near your hotel or a single easy taxi ride back.

Estimated local transport for 2: **JPY 2,500–4,000**
Best balance: Kinkaku-ji is iconic but busy; Ryoan-ji is the better low-crowd alternative if you want more calm.

### Day 4 — April 13: Eastern Kyoto Garden + Farewell Meal
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/moon-stars.svg
- Morning: Ginkaku-ji and the Philosopher’s Path area at an unhurried pace.
- Afternoon: Choose one nearby quieter stop such as Honen-in or Eikan-do if you want a more local-feeling temple visit.
- Food: Final food-focused activity: a kaiseki lunch, tea ceremony, or wagashi tasting.
- Evening: Keep the last night simple with a relaxed dinner and packing time.

Estimated local transport for 2: **JPY 1,800–3,000**
Best balance: This day is ideal for a gentler, less crowded Kyoto feel without losing the classic atmosphere.

## Budget Fit for 2 Adults
### Trip Cost Snapshot
| Category | Estimated Total |
|---|---:|
| Local transport | JPY 7,800–12,700 |
| Attractions / temple entries | JPY 8,000–16,000 |
| Food and drinks | JPY 70,000–110,000 |
| Midrange lodging, 3 nights | JPY 140,000–190,000 |
| Buffer for taxis, snacks, extras | JPY 20,000–35,000 |
| Total estimated trip cost | **JPY 245,800–363,700** |

At a rough planning rate, that usually lands around **USD 1,650–2,450** before international flights, depending mostly on hotel choice and dining style. Your **$2,400 budget** is workable if you stay in a solid midrange hotel and mix casual meals with 1–2 nicer food experiences.

## Crowds vs. Calm: Best Pairings
- **Kiyomizu-dera + Sannenzaka**: go early; it’s the best time-saving way to see a top classic area.
- **Tenryu-ji + Okochi Sanso**: great if you want gardens without a rushed sightseeing feel.
- **Kinkaku-ji + Ryoan-ji**: use Ryoan-ji as the quieter counterpoint to the Golden Pavilion.
- **Ginkaku-ji + Honen-in/Eikan-do**: this is the strongest “popular + less crowded” pairing for a relaxed day.
- **Nishiki Market**: visit mid-afternoon rather than lunch rush if you want easier movement.
